events.title: Estonia's proposed eastern border closures are 'Russophobia,' Russian MFA says

articles.text: News ERR {{1794812100000 | amCalendar}} share Facebook X (Twitter) e-mail Maria Zakharova. Source: SCANPIX / ZUMAPRESS.com / Sergei Karpukhin News Moscow had called plans by Estonia to shut several of its eastern border crossings with Russia after a foiled arson attack attributed to Russia's military intellegence agency "Russophobia." Prime Minister Kristen Michal (Reform) has asked the relevant authorities to prepare the next steps to close the border after a failed bid to start a fire at drone maker Threod Systems on Saturday morning. The Estonian Internal Security Service (ISS/ KAPO) said the act was carried out by residents of Latvia on the orders of Russia's GRU. Russian Foreign Ministry spokeswoman Maria Zakharova told state news agency TASS that if Estonia truly shut its border it would be yet another demonstration of Russophobia. "...If these are their real plans, then they fit into yet another bout of aggressive and unrestrained Russophobia," TASS quoted Zakharova as saying. The Estonian-Russian border runs through Lake Peipus. Border crossing points are highlighted on the map. Source: Helen Wright/ERR/OSM Minister of Foreign Affairs Margus Tsahkna (Eesti 200) said road crossings on the Estonian-Russian border will shut on December 1. There are three crossing points on the border at Narva, Koidula, and Luhamaa. The government is set to discuss the issue later this week. It is not yet known whether the measure will be temporary or indefinite. Saturday's attempted arson attack is the second on a defense industry company in Estonia since August, when Milrem Robotics, which is based in Tallinn, was targeted. KAPO also attributed the incident to the GRU. Similar facilities have also been targeted across Europe as part of a campaign to reduce support for Ukraine and sow fear, the agency said. -- Follow ERR News on Facebook and Twitter and never miss an update! events.title: Estonian security chief: 'I hope Latvia will take sufficient measures'

articles.text: Estonian security chief: 'I hope Latvia will take sufficient measures' Share Follow: Follow LSM on Google Photo: Alamy Stock Photo Igaunijas karogs virs Tallinas Yesterday, 10:09 Defence Authors: LSM English (Latvian Public Media) , ERR News Estonian public media ERR News has an interesting interview with the country's security service chief concerning a recent incident in which eight Latvian nationals were arrested on suspicion of a Russia-backed sabotage plot. In the interview Estonian Internal Security Service (ISS/KAPO) Director General Margo Palloson acknowledges the assistance received from his Latvian counterparts in foiling the plot and also considers the wider implications – which may include the complete closure of Estonia's border with Russia. That in turn could make it advisable for Latvia to follow suit, it is intimated. The whole interview can be read here . Seen a mistake?
